ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure, with a carbonyl/ester-like fragment R–C(=O)–O on the left; this bridging O is connected to the middle carbon. The middle carbon is connected to the N–R3 above by a double bond, and is connected to the adjacent carbon on the right. The adjacent carbon on the right is connected to R2, and is connected to an amine nitrogen; this amine nitrogen is also connected to H and R1. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem asks to ignore the arrows. Reasoning: Count the heavy-atom connections from left to right and do not count bonds involving hydrogen: 1 R–carbonyl C, 2 carbonyl C=O, 3 carbonyl C–O bridge, 4 bridge O–central C, 5 central C=N, 6 N–R3, 7 central C–adjacent carbon, 8 adjacent carbon–R2, 9 adjacent carbon–amine N, 10 amine N–R1. N–H is not counted, arrows are not counted. Therefore the total is 10.

method.method_draft: After describing the image, scan the skeleton left to right and mark each heavy-atom connection: R–carbonyl C, carbonyl C=O, carbonyl C–O bridge, bridge O–central C, central C=N, N–R3, central C–adjacent carbon, adjacent carbon–R2, adjacent carbon–amine N, and amine N–R1. Do not count N–H and do not count arrows. The list contains 10 bonds.
